facts.statement: Igai fossils were first discovered in November 1977 by German researchers Karl Werner Barthel and Ronald Böttcher.
facts.quote: Fossils of Igai were first discovered in early November 1977 by German scientists Kal Werner Barthel and Ronald Böttcher of Technische Universität Berlin (TUB), who had been conducting research for the Sonderforschungsbereiches (Collaborative Research Center) of the TUB.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Kharga Oasis near the town of Baris in the Western Desert of Egypt.
facts.quote: These fossils were unearthed in the Kharga Oasis near the town of Baris in the Western Desert of Egypt.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, VB 621–640, was sent to Germany in 27 plaster jackets after excavation in 1977.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, VB 621–640, was originally excavated in November 1977 by Karl Werner Barthel and Ronald Böttcher of Technische Universität Berlin (TUB) and sent to Germany in 27 plaster jackets.

facts.statement: The partial skeleton's preservation deteriorated due to preparation choices and insufficient storage.
facts.quote: Due to preparation choices and insufficient storage, the partial skeleton's state of preservation decreased.

facts.statement: Most of the Kharga specimen was transferred to the Museum für Naturkunde on September 11, 2008, excluding the left tibia and an isolated femur.
facts.quote: On September 11, 2008, several dinosaur specimens from Egypt and Sudan were transferred to the Museum für Naturkunde, among them most of the Kharga specimen minus the left tibia and an isolated femur.

facts.statement: The remains were formally named the new genus and species Igai semkhu in 2023.
facts.quote: In 2023, they were named as belonging to a new genus and species of titanosaur, Igai semkhu.

facts.statement: The species name semkhu means 'the forgotten' in Ancient Egyptian, alluding to the specimen's complex history and the recent discovery of non-marine Cretaceous vertebrates in continental Africa.
facts.quote: The specific name, "semkhu", is Ancient Egyptian for "the forgotten", referring both to the specimen's convoluted history and the relatively recent discovery of non-marine Cretaceous vertebrates from continental Africa.

facts.statement: Igai lived during the Late Cretaceous in the Quseir Formation of Kharga Oasis, Egypt.
facts.quote: Igai is a genus of titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous Quseir Formation of Kharga Oasis, Egypt.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was found in the Quseir Formation of the Upper Cretaceous in the Jariyá Oasis, Egypt.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la formación Quseir del Cretácico Superior en el oasis de Jariyá, Egipto.

facts.statement: Igai lived approximately 74 to 72 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 74 y 72 millones de años, en el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: Igai is estimated to be 10 to 15 meters long, making it larger than the contemporary Mansourasaurus.
facts.quote: Based on comparisons with other titanosaurs, Igai has been estimated at 10 - 15 m in length, larger than the sympatric Mansourasaurus which was 8 - 10 m long.

facts.statement: Igai semkhu was relatively slender compared to other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Igai semkhu was relatively slender by titanosaur standards.

facts.statement: All preserved vertebrae of Igai feature opisthocoelus centra with large, deep, oval-shaped pleurocoels on their sides.
facts.quote: All preserved vertebrae of Igai have opisthocoelus centra, which bear large, deep, oval-shaped pleurocoels (gaps for air sacs) on their lateral (side) surfaces.

facts.statement: The fifth metacarpal of Igai possesses two distinct tubercles on its medial side not found in other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The fifth metacarpal has two distinct tubercles on its medial side, one near the proximal end and one near the distal end, that are not seen in other titanosaurs.

facts.statement: The first and second metatarsals of Igai display distinct grooves absent in other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The first and second metatarsals show distinct grooves that are not seen in other titanosaurs.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Igai either as a relative of South American titanosaurs or within an Afro-Eurasian clade including Lirainosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia.
facts.quote: Igai was entered into a phylogenetic analysis and found to be in two possible positions: one as a close relative of the South American Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus and another in an Afro-Eurasian clade that includes Lirainosaurus, Opisthocoelicaudia, and the sympatric Mansourasaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers preferred the Afro-Eurasian classification for Igai, supporting the hypothesis that northern African Cretaceous taxa were related to European ones.
facts.quote: The authors preferred the second result since it conforms to a hypothesis that northern African taxa during the Cretaceous were more closely related to European ones while southern African taxa had more Gondwanan origins.

facts.statement: A cladogram illustrates the preferred Afro-Eurasian phylogenetic position for Igai.
facts.quote: El siguiente cladograma muestra la opción afroeurasiática, con los taxones africanos resaltados en rojo.

facts.statement: The genus Igai was named by Gorscak and colleagues in 2023.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Igai (genus), Gorscak et al. 2023

facts.statement: Igai belongs to the dinosaur family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saltasauridae

facts.statement: Igai is classified within the dinosaur class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Igai lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Igai has been recorded so far.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

rejected.quote: The generic name, "Igai", refers to a mysterious "lord of the oasis" worshipped around the Dakhla and Kharga Oases during the Old Kingdom of Egypt.
